# piquelctl commands

This page lists every `piquelctl` command with its arguments and options. It
is generated from the same definitions as `piquelctl --help`, so `--help` on
any command prints the same text. For how to install the CLI, connect it to a
daemon, and read its output, see [piquelctl](cli.md). The
[user guide](../introduction.md) shows the commands at work.

Every command also accepts `-h` (a summary) and `--help` (everything below),
and `piquelctl --version` prints the CLI's version.

## `piquelctl`

Operate a piqueld control plane.

`piquelctl` connects to the daemon's Unix socket, `/run/piqueld/piqueld.sock`, unless `--socket`, `--url`, the `PIQUELD_SOCKET` or `PIQUELD_URL` variable, or a connection profile names another endpoint. It authenticates with `PIQUELD_TOKEN`, or with the login that `piquelctl login` saved. On the daemon host, root and the daemon's user need no login.

```text
piquelctl [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Global options:

- `--profile <NAME>`: Connect with this profile from the profiles files.

  Defaults to `PIQUELD_PROFILE`, else to the profile named `default` if there is one.
- `--profiles-file <PATH>`: Read profiles only from this file.

  Defaults to `PIQUELD_PROFILES_FILE`. Without either, `piquelctl` reads `/etc/piqueld/profiles.toml`, then `~/.config/piqueld/profiles.toml` (in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` when it is set), whose profiles replace those of the same name.
- `--socket <PATH>`: Connect to the daemon's Unix socket at this path.

  It overrides `PIQUELD_SOCKET`, `PIQUELD_URL` and the profile's endpoint. Without any of them, `piquelctl` uses `/run/piqueld/piqueld.sock`.
- `--account <ACCOUNT>`: Act as this saved login, by username or account ID.

  Defaults to the login you saved last for this daemon. `PIQUELD_TOKEN` takes precedence over saved logins.
- `--allow-insecure-http`: Allow sending credentials over plain HTTP to a remote daemon.

  Only use it when something else encrypts the connection, such as Tailscale: `piquelctl` adds no encryption and doesn't check. HTTPS, loopback addresses and the Unix socket don't need it.
- `--url <URL>`: Connect to the daemon over HTTP or HTTPS at this address.

  Give an origin without a path, query or credentials, such as `http://127.0.0.1:7845` or `https://piqueld.example.ts.net`. It overrides `PIQUELD_URL`, `PIQUELD_SOCKET` and the profile's endpoint.
- `--timeout <DURATION>`: Give up on the command after this long, such as `500ms`, `30s`, `2m` or `1h`.

  A number without a unit is seconds. The limit also applies to each request. Confirmation prompts don't count towards it, and it doesn't limit the session of `app exec` and `preview exec`, or how long `login` waits for your approval. `PIQUELD_TIMEOUT` and a profile's `timeout` replace the default. Default: `30s`.
- `--json`: Print the result as JSON on standard output.

  Information, warnings and errors on standard error become one JSON object per line.
- `-q, --quiet`: Hide human-readable results, information and progress.

  JSON results, warnings, errors and prompts still appear.
- `--noninteractive`: Never prompt, even on a terminal.

  Commands that ask for confirmation then fail unless you pass `--yes`.

Commands:

- [`piquelctl login`](#piquelctl-login): Sign in with a passkey through your browser, and save the login.
- [`piquelctl logout`](#piquelctl-logout): Sign out: revoke the current credential and delete its saved copy.
- [`piquelctl whoami`](#piquelctl-whoami): Show who you are signed in as and what the current credential may do.
- [`piquelctl account`](#piquelctl-account): Manage accounts: list them, change their grants, and create invitation and enrollment links.

- [`piquelctl sign-in-link`](#piquelctl-sign-in-link): Print a one-time link that signs a browser in as the host operator.
- [`piquelctl setup-link`](#piquelctl-setup-link): Print the link that creates the first account.
- [`piquelctl profiles`](#piquelctl-profiles): List your connection profiles and their endpoints.
- [`piquelctl secrets`](#piquelctl-secrets): Manage the daemon's encryption key for secrets.

## `piquelctl login`

Sign in with a passkey through your browser, and save the login.

`login` prints a link and a code. Open the link in any browser, even on another machine, and approve the code with your passkey. It waits until the code expires, at most 15 minutes, whatever `--timeout` says. It then saves the login for this daemon in `~/.config/piqueld/credentials.json` (in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` when it is set), or in the file `PIQUELD_CREDENTIALS_FILE` names.

Grant options limit what the login may do; without them, it has all your account's access. Here `--app` takes application IDs, not names, which cannot be looked up before signing in.

```text
piquelctl login [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--preset <PRESET>`: Grant the permissions of this preset.
  - `read-only`: Read applications, their logs and history.
  - `deploy`: Read and deploy applications, such as for CI.
  - `developer`: Everything on applications but deleting them, including running commands in them.
  - `admin`: Every permission, on the selected applications or on the installation.
- `--permission <PERMISSION>`: Grant this permission.

  Repeat it to grant several.
  - `admin`: Every ability, including permissions added later.
  - `apps:read`: Read configuration, status, deployments and secret names.
  - `apps:write`: Edit configuration, apply manifests, rename and add environments.
  - `apps:deploy`: Deploy and reconcile environments, create and deploy previews.
  - `apps:delete`: Delete applications, environments and previews.
  - `previews:deploy`: Create and deploy previews and read their logs.
  - `previews:delete`: Delete and prune previews.
  - `secrets:write`: Store and delete secret values.
  - `logs:read`: Read runtime, build and job logs.
  - `apps:exec`: Run commands in running containers, which can read secret values.
  - `events:read`: Read history, diagnostics and analytics.
  - `apps:create`: Create applications.
  - `system:read`: Read daemon configuration, resources, history and notifications.
  - `system:operate`: Recover the secret key and retry notifications.
  - `accounts:manage`: Manage accounts with equal or less access, and invitations.
  - `audit:read`: Read every account's audit trail.
  - `telemetry:grant`: Grant environments every application's telemetry.
  - `notifications:manage`: Manage notification destinations.
- `--app <APPLICATION_ID>`: Limit the application permissions to this application.

  Repeat it to allow several applications. Without it, the permissions apply to every application. Installation-wide permissions, such as `system:read`, are never limited.

## `piquelctl logout`

Sign out: revoke the current credential and delete its saved copy.

With `PIQUELD_TOKEN` set, it revokes that token and leaves saved logins alone.

```text
piquelctl logout [OPTIONS]
```

## `piquelctl account list`

List the accounts you can see, with their grants.

With `accounts:manage`, that is every account, and the host operator's live browser sessions, which `token revoke` ends. Otherwise, it is only yours.

```text

```

## `piquelctl account access`

Replace an account's grants.

Choose the new grants with `--preset`, `--permission`, or both. Needs `accounts:manage`, every grant the account has, and every grant you give it. An API token can't change grants.

```text
piquelctl account access [OPTIONS] <ACCOUNT>
```

- `<ACCOUNT>`: Account username or ID.

  - `previews:delete`: Delete and prune previews.
  - `secrets:write`: Store and delete secret values.
  - `logs:read`: Read runtime, build and job logs.
  - `apps:exec`: Run commands in running containers, which can read secret values.
  - `events:read`: Read history, diagnostics and analytics.

## `piquelctl account enroll`

Print a link that adds a passkey to an existing account.

The link works once within 24 hours, and signs in whoever uses it as that account. Anyone may create one for their own account; another account needs `accounts:manage` and every grant it has. An API token or limited login can't create enrollment links.

```text
piquelctl account enroll [OPTIONS] <ACCOUNT>
```

Arguments:

- `<ACCOUNT>`: Account username or ID.

## `piquelctl token`

Create, list and revoke your API tokens and sessions.

```text
piquelctl token [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Commands:

- [`piquelctl token create`](#piquelctl-token-create): Create an API token for your account, and print it.
- [`piquelctl token list`](#piquelctl-token-list): List your sessions and API tokens, with their grants and expiry.
- [`piquelctl token revoke`](#piquelctl-token-revoke): Revoke a session or API token by ID.

## `piquelctl token create`

Create an API token for your account, and print it.

The token has only the grants you select, with `--preset`, `--permission`, or both, and you must hold them. Use it with `PIQUELD_TOKEN`. Keep it safe: it is printed once and never shown again. An API token can't create tokens.

```text
piquelctl token create [OPTIONS] <NAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME>`: Token name, up to 200 bytes.

Options:

- `--preset <PRESET>`: Grant the permissions of this preset.
  - `read-only`: Read applications, their logs and history.
  - `deploy`: Read and deploy applications, such as for CI.
  - `developer`: Everything on applications but deleting them, including running commands in them.
  - `admin`: Every permission, on the selected applications or on the installation.
- `--permission <PERMISSION>`: Grant this permission.

  Repeat it to grant several.
  - `admin`: Every ability, including permissions added later.
  - `apps:read`: Read configuration, status, deployments and secret names.
  - `apps:write`: Edit configuration, apply manifests, rename and add environments.
  - `apps:deploy`: Deploy and reconcile environments, create and deploy previews.
  - `apps:delete`: Delete applications, environments and previews.
  - `previews:deploy`: Create and deploy previews and read their logs.
  - `previews:delete`: Delete and prune previews.
  - `secrets:write`: Store and delete secret values.
  - `logs:read`: Read runtime, build and job logs.
  - `apps:exec`: Run commands in running containers, which can read secret values.
  - `events:read`: Read history, diagnostics and analytics.
  - `apps:create`: Create applications.
  - `system:read`: Read daemon configuration, resources, history and notifications.
  - `system:operate`: Recover the secret key and retry notifications.
  - `accounts:manage`: Manage accounts with equal or less access, and invitations.
  - `audit:read`: Read every account's audit trail.
  - `telemetry:grant`: Grant environments every application's telemetry.
  - `notifications:manage`: Manage notification destinations.
- `--app <NAME_OR_ID>`: Limit the application permissions to this application.

  Repeat it to allow several applications. Without it, the permissions apply to every application. Installation-wide permissions, such as `system:read`, are never limited.
- `--days <DAYS>`: Expire the token after this many days, from 1.

  The daemon refuses more days than its `auth.max_token_days`. Default: `90`.
- `--no-expiry`: Never expire the token.

  The daemon refuses it when it sets `auth.max_token_days`.
- `--tailnet <USER_OR_TAG>`: Accept the token only over the tailnet, from this user's devices or devices with this tag.

  Give a login name, such as `alice@example.com`, or a tag, such as `tag:ci`. The daemon needs its tailnet node or a private dashboard hostname.

## `piquelctl token list`

List your sessions and API tokens, with their grants and expiry.

```text
piquelctl token list [OPTIONS]
```

## `piquelctl token revoke`

Revoke a session or API token by ID.

Give the ID of one of yours, from `token list`, or of a host operator browser session, from `account list`.

```text
piquelctl token revoke [OPTIONS] <ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<ID>`: Credential ID.

## `piquelctl audit`

Read the audit trail of API requests, newest first.

Each line is one request: when it was made, its outcome and status, what it did and to which application or environment, who made it with which credential, and from where. With `audit:read`, you see every account's requests. Without it, you see only your own account's, and an API token only its own.

```text
piquelctl audit [OPTIONS]
       piquelctl audit <COMMAND>
```

Options:

- `--user <ACCOUNT>`: Only show the requests of this account, by username or ID, even a deleted one.

  Accounts other than yours need `audit:read`. Unlike the global `--account`, it doesn't choose the login you read with.
- `--credential <CREDENTIAL>`: Only show the requests made with this credential ID, from `token list`.
- `--outcome <OUTCOME>`: Only show the requests with this outcome.
  - `allowed`: Authorized, and succeeded.
  - `denied`: Refused: missing credentials or permission, or a target hidden from the caller.
  - `failed`: Authorized, but failed.
- `--cursor <CURSOR>`: Read the page after this cursor, which the previous page printed.
- `--limit <LIMIT>`: Show at most this many requests, from 1 to 100. Default: `50`.

Commands:

- [`piquelctl audit verify`](#piquelctl-audit-verify): Check that no one altered the audit trail.

## `piquelctl audit verify`

Check that no one altered the audit trail.

It checks the trail's hash chain, and exits with code 3 when a record was edited, inserted or removed. It prints the newest link: keep it elsewhere to also detect that the newest records were removed. Needs `audit:read`.

```text
piquelctl audit verify [OPTIONS]
```

## `piquelctl recover-admin`

Print a one-time link that creates a new administrator account.

Use it to regain access when no administrator can sign in. Run it on the daemon host as root or as the daemon's user, such as with `sudo`: the daemon serves it only over its Unix socket. The link works once within 24 hours and replaces any earlier one. Issuing it raises a security notification.

```text
piquelctl recover-admin [OPTIONS]
```

## `piquelctl sign-in-link`

Print a one-time link that signs a browser in as the host operator.

The browser gets full access for 12 hours. The link works once within 10 minutes. Run it on the daemon host as root or as the daemon's user, without `PIQUELD_TOKEN` or a saved login: the daemon serves it only over its Unix socket, to the host operator. Issuing it raises a security notification.

```text
piquelctl sign-in-link [OPTIONS]
```

## `piquelctl setup-link`

Print the link that creates the first account.

Run it on the daemon host: the daemon serves it only over its Unix socket, and only until the first account exists.

```text
piquelctl setup-link [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--open`: Also open the link in your default browser.

## `piquelctl profiles`

```text
piquelctl profiles [OPTIONS]
```

## `piquelctl secrets`

Manage the daemon's encryption key for secrets.

```text
piquelctl secrets [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Commands:

- [`piquelctl secrets recover-key`](#piquelctl-secrets-recover-key): Recover from a lost secret key by discarding every value it encrypted.

## `piquelctl secrets recover-key`

Recover from a lost secret key by discarding every value it encrypted.

Use it only when the daemon's `secrets.key` is lost and you have no backup: the daemon refuses while the key still works. It discards the stored and generated secret values of ALL applications and environments and the repository webhook secrets, and deletes every notification destination, since their URLs are encrypted. Running services keep their Docker secrets. Afterwards, set the stored secrets again and deploy, which also generates new values for generated secrets, give each repository a new webhook secret with `app repository webhook rotate`, and add the notification destinations again with `notification set`. Needs `system:operate`.

```text
piquelctl secrets recover-key [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt.

## `piquelctl notification`

## `piquelctl notification list`

List notification destinations and what each receives.

Their URLs are never shown. Needs `system:read` or `notifications:manage`.

```text
piquelctl notification list [OPTIONS]
```

## `piquelctl notification set`

Create a notification destination, or change one.

Options you omit keep the current settings. A new destination needs `--url-file` or `--url-stdin`. It receives every category but `deployment_succeeded`, about every application, without previews. Changing its URL or kind cancels its pending deliveries. Needs `notifications:manage`.

```text
piquelctl notification set [OPTIONS] <NAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME>`: Destination name.

Options:

- `--kind <KIND>`: Payload format.

  A new destination defaults to `json`.
  - `json`: Versioned JSON describing the event.
  - `discord`: A Discord webhook message.
- `--url-file <PATH>`: Read the webhook URL from this file.
- `--url-stdin`: Read the webhook URL from standard input.
- `--enabled <BOOL>`: Whether to send notifications.

  `false` pauses the destination and cancels its pending deliveries. `true` resumes it, without sending what happened meanwhile. Values: `true`, `false`.
- `--categories <CATEGORIES>`: Receive only these categories: comma-separated, or `''` for none.

  A category that stays keeps its message. Values: `build_failures`, `deployment_failures`, `service_degradation`, `daemon_failures`, `recovery`, `security`, `daemon_started`, `deployment_succeeded`.
- `--message <CATEGORY=TEXT>`: Send TEXT with each notification of CATEGORY, and receive that category.

  TEXT has 1 to 1000 characters, such as a Discord role mention `<@&ROLE_ID>`. CATEGORY is one of the values `--categories` accepts. Repeat it for several categories.
- `--no-message <CATEGORY>`: Stop sending text with this category's notifications.

  Repeat it for several categories. Values: `build_failures`, `deployment_failures`, `service_degradation`, `daemon_failures`, `recovery`, `security`, `daemon_started`, `deployment_succeeded`.
- `--apps <APPS>`: Receive notifications only about these applications: comma-separated names or IDs, or `''` for none.

  Daemon-wide notifications, such as daemon failures and security events, arrive either way.
- `--all-apps`: Receive notifications about every application, including ones created later.
- `--previews <BOOL>`: Whether to receive notifications about previews. Values: `true`, `false`.

## `piquelctl notification test`

Send a test notification to a destination now.

It fails unless the receiver acknowledges it. The test skips the delivery queue and history. Needs `notifications:manage`.

```text
piquelctl notification test [OPTIONS] <NAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME>`: Destination name.

## `piquelctl notification delete`

Delete a notification destination and cancel its pending deliveries.

The delivery history keeps its name. Needs `notifications:manage`.

```text
piquelctl notification delete [OPTIONS] <NAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME>`: Destination name.

Options:

- `-y, --yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt.

## `piquelctl notification deliveries`

List notification deliveries, newest first.

Needs `system:read`.

```text
piquelctl notification deliveries [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--cursor <CURSOR>`: Read the page after this cursor, which the previous page printed.

## `piquelctl notification retry`

Try a failed delivery again, with the destination's current settings.

Needs `system:operate`.

```text
piquelctl notification retry [OPTIONS] <ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<ID>`: Delivery ID, from `notification deliveries`.

## `piquelctl dns refresh`

Check every DNS provider's credentials and zones now.

The daemon otherwise checks them every hour. It reads credential files only when it starts, so restart it after changing one. Needs `system:operate`.

```text
piquelctl dns refresh [OPTIONS]
```

## `piquelctl app`

Create, inspect, edit and deploy applications.

```text
piquelctl app [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Commands:

- [`piquelctl app create`](#piquelctl-app-create): Create an empty application.

- [`piquelctl app list`](#piquelctl-app-list): List applications with their environments and status.
- [`piquelctl app show`](#piquelctl-app-show): Show an application and its environments.
- [`piquelctl app logs`](#piquelctl-app-logs): Show recent Docker logs of the application's only environment.
- [`piquelctl app exec`](#piquelctl-app-exec): Run a one-off command in a running task of a service.
- [`piquelctl app secret`](#piquelctl-app-secret): Manage the application's stored secrets and who may mount them.
- [`piquelctl app validate`](#piquelctl-app-validate): Check a TOML manifest locally, without contacting a daemon.
- [`piquelctl app plan`](#piquelctl-app-plan): Show what saving a TOML manifest would change, without saving it.
- [`piquelctl app apply`](#piquelctl-app-apply): Save a TOML manifest, creating or replacing the application it names.
- [`piquelctl app delete`](#piquelctl-app-delete): Delete an application with all its environments and previews.
- [`piquelctl app reconcile`](#piquelctl-app-reconcile): Retry the latest operation of the application's only environment.
- [`piquelctl app deploy`](#piquelctl-app-deploy): Deploy the application's only environment.
- [`piquelctl app rename`](#piquelctl-app-rename): Rename an application.
- [`piquelctl app manifest`](#piquelctl-app-manifest): Print the saved manifest as TOML.
- [`piquelctl app releases`](#piquelctl-app-releases): List the application's releases, newest first.

## `piquelctl app create`

Create an empty application.

Add services, volumes and routes to it with the other `app` commands. Needs `apps:create`.

```text
piquelctl app create [OPTIONS] <NAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME>`: Name of the new application, unused by any other.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt.

## `piquelctl app service`

Add, change and remove an application's services.

```text
piquelctl app service [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Commands:

- [`piquelctl app service add`](#piquelctl-app-service-add): Add a service that runs an image, or builds a Git repository with `--git`.
- [`piquelctl app service remove`](#piquelctl-app-service-remove): Remove a service.
- [`piquelctl app service rename`](#piquelctl-app-service-rename): Rename a service.
- [`piquelctl app service replicas`](#piquelctl-app-service-replicas): Set the number of replicas the service runs.
- [`piquelctl app service source`](#piquelctl-app-service-source): Set where the service's image comes from: a prebuilt image or a Git build.
- [`piquelctl app service env`](#piquelctl-app-service-env): Set or remove one environment variable of a service.
- [`piquelctl app service command`](#piquelctl-app-service-command): Replace the image's entrypoint with the elements after `--`.
- [`piquelctl app service arguments`](#piquelctl-app-service-arguments): Replace the image's default arguments with the elements after `--`.
- [`piquelctl app service depends-on`](#piquelctl-app-service-depends-on): Set the services that must be healthy before this one rolls out.
- [`piquelctl app service rollout`](#piquelctl-app-service-rollout): Set the order and monitor window of the service's rollouts.
- [`piquelctl app service telemetry`](#piquelctl-app-service-telemetry): Choose whether the service receives the daemon's own telemetry.
- [`piquelctl app service mount`](#piquelctl-app-service-mount): Mount a volume into a service, or remove a mount.
- [`piquelctl app service health`](#piquelctl-app-service-health): Set, change, or remove a service's health check.
- [`piquelctl app service cpu`](#piquelctl-app-service-cpu): Set the service's CPU limit, or remove it with `--clear`.
- [`piquelctl app service memory`](#piquelctl-app-service-memory): Set the service's memory limit, or remove it with `--clear`.

## `piquelctl app service add`

Add a service that runs an image, or builds a Git repository with `--git`.

The new service runs one replica and has no other settings. Adding a service whose name is taken fails.

```text
piquelctl app service add [OPTIONS] <APP> <SERVICE> [IMAGE]
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<SERVICE>`: Service name.
- `[IMAGE]`: Image to run, such as `nginx:stable`. It may reference variables. Omit it when you pass `--git`.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.
- `--git <URL>`: Build this Git repository with Docker instead of running an image. It takes a clone URL, or a path on the daemon's host.
- `--branch <BRANCH>`: Branch to build when no commit is pinned. Default: `main`.
- `--commit <COMMIT>`: Build this full commit hash instead of the branch head.
- `--dockerfile <PATH>`: Dockerfile path, relative to the repository root. Default: `Dockerfile`.
- `--context <PATH>`: Build context directory, relative to the repository root. Default: `.`.
- `--build-arg <KEY=VALUE>`: Docker build argument. Repeat it to set several. Values aren't secret: Docker records them in the image.
- `--target <STAGE>`: Dockerfile stage to build. By default, Docker builds the last stage.

## `piquelctl app service remove`

Remove a service.

Its routes, jobs and export are removed with it, and other services stop depending on it. The volumes it mounts keep their data.

```text
piquelctl app service remove [OPTIONS] <APP> <SERVICE>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<SERVICE>`: Service name.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.

## `piquelctl app service command`

Replace the image's entrypoint with the elements after `--`.

Put the command's options before `--`. Without elements, the service uses the image's own entrypoint.

```text
piquelctl app service command [OPTIONS] <APP> <SERVICE> [-- <COMMAND>...]
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<SERVICE>`: Service name.
- `[COMMAND]...`: Entrypoint elements, after `--`. Each one is passed as is, spaces included, and may reference variables.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.

Replace the image's default arguments with the elements after `--`.

Put the command's options before `--`. Without elements, the service uses the image's own arguments.

```text
piquelctl app service arguments [OPTIONS] <APP> <SERVICE> [-- <ARGUMENTS>...]
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<SERVICE>`: Service name.
- `[ARGUMENTS]...`: Argument elements, after `--`. Each one is passed as is, spaces included, and may reference variables.

- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.

- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.

List them after `--`. Without any, the service depends on none. Jobs of the service wait for them too.

```text
piquelctl app service depends-on [OPTIONS] <APP> <SERVICE> [-- <SERVICES>...]
```

Arguments:

- `<SERVICE>`: Service name.

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.

## `piquelctl app service rollout`

Set the order and monitor window of the service's rollouts.

A flag you omit returns to its default, so running it without flags restores both defaults.

```text
piquelctl app service rollout [OPTIONS] <APP> <SERVICE>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<SERVICE>`: Service name.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.
- `--order <ORDER>`: `stop-first` stops the old task before starting its replacement, and `start-first` starts the replacement first. By default, the order is `stop-first` when the service mounts a volume writable, else `start-first`.
- `--monitor-seconds <SECONDS>`: Seconds Docker watches each replacement task for failure, from 1 to 3600. By default, 30.

## `piquelctl app service telemetry`

Choose whether the service receives the daemon's own telemetry.

With `on`, the service receives the traces, metrics and logs of every application on a socket mounted at `/run/piqueld/telemetry`, in environments granted telemetry with `env telemetry`. At most one service per application can receive it, and it must run one replica.

```text
piquelctl app service telemetry [OPTIONS] <APP> <SERVICE> <on|off>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<SERVICE>`: Service name.
- `<on|off>`: `on` to receive telemetry where the environment is granted it, `off` to never receive it. Values: `on`, `off`.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.

## `piquelctl app service health`

Set, change, or remove a service's health check.

The commands that change one setting need a health check of the matching kind first.

```text
piquelctl app service health [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Commands:

- [`piquelctl app service health http`](#piquelctl-app-service-health-http): Replace the health check with an HTTP check.
- [`piquelctl app service health command`](#piquelctl-app-service-health-command): Replace the health check with a command, given after `--`.
- [`piquelctl app service health clear`](#piquelctl-app-service-health-clear): Remove the health check.
- [`piquelctl app service health port`](#piquelctl-app-service-health-port): Change the port of an HTTP health check.
- [`piquelctl app service health path`](#piquelctl-app-service-health-path): Change the request path of an HTTP health check.
- [`piquelctl app service health command-elements`](#piquelctl-app-service-health-command-elements): Change the command of a command health check, given after `--`.
- [`piquelctl app service health interval`](#piquelctl-app-service-health-interval): Change the seconds between health checks.
- [`piquelctl app service health timeout`](#piquelctl-app-service-health-timeout): Change the seconds before a health check counts as failed.
- [`piquelctl app service health start-period`](#piquelctl-app-service-health-start-period): Change the seconds after the container starts during which failed checks don't count.
- [`piquelctl app service health retries`](#piquelctl-app-service-health-retries): Change how many consecutive failed checks make the container unhealthy.

## `piquelctl app service health http`

Replace the health check with an HTTP check.

The check sends a `GET` request to the port inside the container and passes on a 2xx or 3xx status. It needs nothing in the image.

```text
piquelctl app service health http [OPTIONS] <APP> <SERVICE> <PORT>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<SERVICE>`: Service name.
- `<PORT>`: Container port to probe, from 1 to 65535.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.
- `--path <PATH>`: Request path, starting with `/`. Default: `/health`.
- `--interval <SECONDS>`: Seconds between checks, from 1 to 3600. Default: `10`.
- `--check-timeout <SECONDS>`: Seconds before a check counts as failed, from 1 to the interval. Default: `3`.
- `--start-period <SECONDS>`: Seconds after the container starts during which failed checks don't count, up to 3600. A passing check makes the container healthy at once. Default: `0`.
- `--retries <RETRIES>`: Consecutive failed checks that make the container unhealthy, from 1 to 100. Default: `3`.

## `piquelctl app service health command`

- `--interval <SECONDS>`: Seconds between checks, from 1 to 3600. Default: `10`.

- `--start-period <SECONDS>`: Seconds after the container starts during which failed checks don't count, up to 3600. A passing check makes the container healthy at once. Default: `0`.
- `--retries <RETRIES>`: Consecutive failed checks that make the container unhealthy, from 1 to 100. Default: `3`.

## `piquelctl app file add`

Mount a read-only file into a service, replacing any file at the same path.

Give its content with exactly one of `--content`, `--from` or `--path`. A file holds at most 500 KiB and can't be empty.

```text
piquelctl app file add [OPTIONS] <--content <TEXT>|--from <LOCAL_FILE>|--path <REPOSITORY_PATH>> <APP> <SERVICE> <TARGET>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<SERVICE>`: Service name.
- `<TARGET>`: Absolute container path of the file.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.
- `--content <TEXT>`: The file's content. Variables in it are never rendered.
- `--from <LOCAL_FILE>`: Read the content from this local file now, and save it in the manifest.
- `--path <REPOSITORY_PATH>`: Read the content from this file in the manifest's repository, relative to its root, each time a deployment fetches the manifest. Only repository-backed applications can use it.
- `--mode <MODE>`: Octal permissions of the file, from `0000` to `0777`, such as `0440`. Root owns the file. Default: `0444`.

## `piquelctl app route add`

Add an HTTPS route to a service.

```text
piquelctl app route add [OPTIONS] <APP> <HOSTNAME> <SERVICE> <PORT>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<HOSTNAME>`: Hostname of the route: an exact name, or a wildcard such as `*.example.com`. It may reference variables, such as `${{ vars.domain }}`.
- `<SERVICE>`: Service that serves the route.
- `<PORT>`: HTTP port the service listens on inside its container.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.
- `--visibility <VISIBILITY>`: `public` serves everyone, `private` only devices on the tailnet. The environment's visibility ceiling can make it stricter. Default: `private`. Values: `public`, `private`.
- `--name <NAME>`: Stable route name, unique within the application. It selects the route in every environment and preview, such as with `env url --route`.

## `piquelctl app route redirect`

Add an HTTPS route that the gateway answers with a redirect.

```text
piquelctl app route redirect [OPTIONS] <APP> <HOSTNAME> <URL>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<HOSTNAME>`: Hostname of the route: an exact name, or a wildcard such as `*.example.com`. It may reference variables, such as `${{ vars.domain }}`.
- `<URL>`: Destination: an absolute `http` or `https` URL, without query or fragment. It may reference variables.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.
- `--status <STATUS>`: HTTP status of the redirect: `301`, `302`, `303`, `307` or `308`. Default: `308`.
- `--no-preserve-path`: Drop the request path and query instead of appending them to the destination.
- `--visibility <VISIBILITY>`: `public` serves everyone, `private` only devices on the tailnet. The environment's visibility ceiling can make it stricter. Default: `private`. Values: `public`, `private`.
- `--name <NAME>`: Stable route name, unique within the application. It selects the route in every environment and preview, such as with `env url --route`.

## `piquelctl app job set`

Add a job that runs before each rollout, or replace the job with this name.

A new job runs after the existing ones, and a replaced job keeps its position. Jobs run in order, after their service's dependencies are healthy, and the other services wait until every job succeeds.

```text
piquelctl app job set [OPTIONS] <APP> <JOB> <SERVICE> -- <COMMAND>...
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<JOB>`: Job name.
- `<SERVICE>`: Service whose image, environment, secrets, mounts and startup dependencies the job reuses.
- `<COMMAND>...`: Command the job runs, after `--`. It replaces the service's command and arguments.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.
- `--timeout-seconds <SECONDS>`: Seconds the job may run before it fails the deployment, from 1 to 86400. By default, the job's current timeout, or 300 for a new job.
- `--volume-access <ACCESS>`: How the job mounts its service's volumes. By default, the job's current access, or `read-only` for a new job.
  - `read-only`: Mount every volume read-only, so the job runs beside the services.
  - `exclusive`: Keep writable volumes writable, and stop every service that mounts one until the rollout.
- `--env <KEY=VALUE>`: Environment variable for the job only, added to its service's. Repeat it to set several. They replace the job's own variables, which it keeps when you pass none.
- `--clear-env`: Remove the job's own environment variables.
- `--secret <NAME=TARGET>`: Secret for the job only, in addition to its service's, mounted at `TARGET`, an absolute path under `/run/secrets/` such as `/run/secrets/db`. Repeat it to mount several. They replace the job's own secrets, which it keeps when you pass none.
- `--clear-secrets`: Remove the job's own secrets.

- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.

- [`piquelctl app export set`](#piquelctl-app-export-set): Export a service to other applications, or replace who may import it.
- [`piquelctl app export remove`](#piquelctl-app-export-remove): Stop exporting a service.

## `piquelctl app export list`

List the services the application exports, as saved.

```text
piquelctl app export list [OPTIONS] <APP>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.

## `piquelctl app export set`

Export a service to other applications, or replace who may import it.

Their services reach it as `<service>.<application>` once both sides have deployed the link.

```text
piquelctl app export set [OPTIONS] --applications <APPS> <APP> <SERVICE>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<SERVICE>`: Service of the application to export.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.
- `--applications <APPS>`: Applications whose environments may import the service. Separate several with commas, or repeat the option. Required.
- `--previews`: Let previews of those applications import it too. Without it, previews can't, even if they could before.

## `piquelctl app export remove`

Stop exporting a service.

```text
piquelctl app export remove [OPTIONS] <APP> <SERVICE>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<SERVICE>`: Service of the application to export.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.

## `piquelctl app import`

Reach the services other applications export, as `<service>.<application>`.
