```text
piquelctl app import [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Commands:

- [`piquelctl app import list`](#piquelctl-app-import-list): List the services the application imports, as saved.
- [`piquelctl app import add`](#piquelctl-app-import-add): Import another application's exported service, or change the environment it reaches.
- [`piquelctl app import remove`](#piquelctl-app-import-remove): Stop importing a service.

## `piquelctl app import list`

List the services the application imports, as saved.

`env show` reports whether each one connects.

```text
piquelctl app import list [OPTIONS] <APP>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.

## `piquelctl app import add`

Import another application's exported service, or change the environment it reaches.

The application's services reach it as `<service>.<application>` once both sides have deployed the link.

```text
piquelctl app import add [OPTIONS] <APP> <APPLICATION> <SERVICE>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<APPLICATION>`: Application that exports the service.
- `<SERVICE>`: Exported service of that application.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.
- `--environment <ENV>`: Environment of the exporting application to reach, such as `staging` or `${{ vars.auth_env }}`. By default, the one named like the importing environment.

## `piquelctl app import remove`

Stop importing a service.

```text
piquelctl app import remove [OPTIONS] <APP> <APPLICATION> <SERVICE>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<APPLICATION>`: Application that exports the service.
- `<SERVICE>`: Exported service of that application.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.

## `piquelctl app variable`

Set and remove manifest variables, and their values per environment and for previews.

```text
piquelctl app variable [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Commands:

- [`piquelctl app variable set`](#piquelctl-app-variable-set): Set a variable's default value, or its value in one environment or in previews.
- [`piquelctl app variable unset`](#piquelctl-app-variable-unset): Remove a variable's default value, or its value in one environment or in previews.

## `piquelctl app variable set`

Set a variable's default value, or its value in one environment or in previews.

An environment's or the previews' value overrides the default.

```text
piquelctl app variable set [OPTIONS] <APP> <NAME> <VALUE>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<NAME>`: Variable name, referenced as `${{ vars.<name> }}`.
- `<VALUE>`: `true`, `false` and integers keep their type, and anything else is text. Text may reference system variables, such as `${{ env.name }}`. Text in double quotes stays text, without the quotes.

Options:

- `--env <ENV>`: Change the variable's value in this environment instead of its default. The environment must exist.
- `--previews`: Change the variable's value in every preview, `[spec.previews.variables]`, instead of its default.
- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.
- `--string`: Keep the value as text even when it looks like a boolean or an integer.

## `piquelctl app variable unset`

Remove a variable's default value, or its value in one environment or in previews.

Removing a value that isn't set fails.

```text
piquelctl app variable unset [OPTIONS] <APP> <NAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<NAME>`: Variable name, referenced as `${{ vars.<name> }}`.

Options:

- `--env <ENV>`: Change the variable's value in this environment instead of its default. The environment must exist.
- `--previews`: Change the variable's value in every preview, `[spec.previews.variables]`, instead of its default.
- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.

## `piquelctl app repository`

Connect the application to a manifest in Git, and manage that connection.

```text
piquelctl app repository [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Commands:

- [`piquelctl app repository connect`](#piquelctl-app-repository-connect): Connect the application to a manifest file in a Git repository.
- [`piquelctl app repository disconnect`](#piquelctl-app-repository-disconnect): Stop reading the manifest from Git, keeping the saved manifest.
- [`piquelctl app repository url`](#piquelctl-app-repository-url): Change the repository every environment fetches the manifest from.
- [`piquelctl app repository path`](#piquelctl-app-repository-path): Change the manifest file every environment reads.
- [`piquelctl app repository sync`](#piquelctl-app-repository-sync): Choose whether environments and previews deploy pushes.
- [`piquelctl app repository reset`](#piquelctl-app-repository-reset): Discard the edits made since the manifest was last read from the repository, saving that manifest again.
- [`piquelctl app repository webhook`](#piquelctl-app-repository-webhook): Show the GitHub webhook that reports pushes, or generate its secret.

## `piquelctl app repository connect`

Connect the application to a manifest file in a Git repository.

Deployments then fetch the manifest from the repository. Every environment follows `--branch`, as do environments created later without their own, unless the manifest declares the environment's branch. Change an environment's branch with `env branch`. You can still edit the application: deployments of the connection's branch deploy your edits until a push changes the manifest file.

```text
piquelctl app repository connect [OPTIONS] <APP> <URL> <PATH>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<URL>`: Git clone URL, or a path on the daemon's host.
- `<PATH>`: Path of the manifest file, relative to the repository root.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.
- `--branch <BRANCH>`: Branch the environments follow. Default: `main`.
- `--commit <COMMIT>`: Pin this full commit hash instead of following the branch.
- `--sync <MODE>`: Whether to deploy pushes, as `app repository sync` sets it. Default: `off`.
  - `off`: Deploy only when asked.
  - `poll`: List the branches every `--interval` seconds.
  - `webhook`: List the branches when GitHub reports a push (see `app repository webhook`).
- `--interval <SECONDS>`: Seconds between polls with `--sync poll`, from 60 to 86400. By default, 300.

## `piquelctl app repository disconnect`

Stop reading the manifest from Git, keeping the saved manifest.

Edits are kept, and environments that followed a branch deploy the saved manifest. Declared environments lose their `branch`, `commit` and `sync`. It fails while services mount files from the repository: give them inline content first.

```text
piquelctl app repository disconnect [OPTIONS] <APP>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.

## `piquelctl app repository url`

Change the repository every environment fetches the manifest from.

```text
piquelctl app repository url [OPTIONS] <APP> <URL>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<URL>`: Git clone URL, or a path on the daemon's host.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.

## `piquelctl app repository path`

Change the manifest file every environment reads.

```text
piquelctl app repository path [OPTIONS] <APP> <PATH>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<PATH>`: Path of the manifest file, relative to the repository root.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.

## `piquelctl app repository sync`

Choose whether environments and previews deploy pushes.

While sync is on, every preview, and every environment that opted in with `env sync` and follows an unpinned branch, redeploys when its branch moves past the head of its last deployment.

```text
piquelctl app repository sync [OPTIONS] <APP> <MODE>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<MODE>`: How to detect pushes.
  - `off`: Deploy only when asked.
  - `poll`: List the branches every `--interval` seconds.
  - `webhook`: List the branches when GitHub reports a push (see `app repository webhook`).

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.
- `--interval <SECONDS>`: Seconds between polls with `poll`, from 60 to 86400. By default, 300.

## `piquelctl app repository reset`

Discard the edits made since the manifest was last read from the repository, saving that manifest again.

`app show` lists the edits. Deployments of the connection's branch then deploy the manifest as read, until a push changes it.

```text
piquelctl app repository reset [OPTIONS] <APP>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.

## `piquelctl app repository webhook`

Show the GitHub webhook that reports pushes, or generate its secret.

```text
piquelctl app repository webhook [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Commands:

- [`piquelctl app repository webhook show`](#piquelctl-app-repository-webhook-show): Show the payload URL to configure in GitHub, and when the secret was generated.
- [`piquelctl app repository webhook rotate`](#piquelctl-app-repository-webhook-rotate): Generate a new webhook secret, replacing the previous one, and print it.

## `piquelctl app repository webhook show`

Show the payload URL to configure in GitHub, and when the secret was generated.

The URL appears once the daemon sets `ingress.webhook_hostname`.

```text
piquelctl app repository webhook show [OPTIONS] <APP>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.

## `piquelctl app repository webhook rotate`

Generate a new webhook secret, replacing the previous one, and print it.

The previous secret stops working at once. The new one is shown only this time.

```text
piquelctl app repository webhook rotate [OPTIONS] <APP>
```

Arguments:

- `<APP>`: Application name or stable ID.

Options:

- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.

## `piquelctl app list`

List applications with their environments and status.

```text
piquelctl app list [OPTIONS]
```

## `piquelctl app show`

Show an application and its environments.

```text
piquelctl app show [OPTIONS] <NAME_OR_ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME_OR_ID>`: Application name or stable ID.

## `piquelctl app logs`

Show recent Docker logs of the application's only environment.

With several environments, use `env logs`. Needs `logs:read`.

```text
piquelctl app logs [OPTIONS] <NAME_OR_ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME_OR_ID>`: Application name or stable ID.

Options:

- `--service <SERVICE>`: Only show this service's output.

  Defaults to every service.
- `--tail <TAIL>`: Show at most this many of the most recent lines, from 1 to 1000, merged across services. Default: `200`.
- `--since-seconds <SECONDS>`: Only show output written within this many seconds, from 1 to 86400 (a day). Default: `3600`.

## `piquelctl app exec`

Run a one-off command in a running task of a service.

The command shares the task's image, environment, secrets, mounts and networks. Its output streams to your terminal, and `piquelctl` exits with its exit code. Stopping `piquelctl` early closes the stream, but the command may keep running. `--timeout` limits connecting, not the session. Needs `apps:exec`.

```text
piquelctl app exec [OPTIONS] <NAME_OR_ID> <SERVICE> -- <COMMAND>...
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME_OR_ID>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<SERVICE>`: Service that runs the command, in one of its running tasks.
- `<COMMAND>...`: Program to run and its arguments, after `--`.

Options:

- `--env <ENV>`: Environment name or stable ID.

  Optional when the application has only one.
- `-i, --interactive`: Forward standard input to the command.
- `-t, --tty`: Allocate a terminal, for interactive programs such as a shell.

  It implies `--interactive`, and needs a terminal on standard input, which it switches to raw mode so that keys such as Ctrl-C reach the command.

## `piquelctl app secret`

Manage the application's stored secrets and who may mount them.

Values are write-only: no command prints them back.

```text
piquelctl app secret [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> <COMMAND>
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.

Commands:

- [`piquelctl app secret list`](#piquelctl-app-secret-list): List the application's stored secrets and who may mount them.
- [`piquelctl app secret set`](#piquelctl-app-secret-set): Create or replace a stored secret.
- [`piquelctl app secret access`](#piquelctl-app-secret-access): Change which environments, and whether previews, may mount a stored secret.
- [`piquelctl app secret delete`](#piquelctl-app-secret-delete): Delete a stored secret and the Docker secrets made from it.

## `piquelctl app secret list`

List the application's stored secrets and who may mount them.

It shows each secret's version, never its value.

```text
piquelctl app secret <APPLICATION> list [OPTIONS]
```

## `piquelctl app secret set`

Create or replace a stored secret.

The value, of 1 to 512000 bytes, comes from a file or standard input, never from an argument. Running services keep their value until the next deployment. A new secret may be mounted by every environment and no preview, unless you set its access. Needs `secrets:write`.

```text
piquelctl app secret <APPLICATION> set [OPTIONS] <NAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME>`: Secret name.

Options:

- `--file <PATH>`: Read the value from this file.
- `--stdin`: Read the value from standard input.
- `--environments <ENVIRONMENTS>`: Let only these environments mount the secret: comma-separated names or IDs, or `''` for none.
- `--all-environments`: Let every environment mount the secret, including ones created later.

  It never includes previews.
- `--previews`: Let previews mount the secret.
- `--no-previews`: Stop previews from mounting the secret.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Fail unless the secret is at this generation; `0` requires that it doesn't exist.

  Defaults to the generation it inspects, or `0` for a new secret.
- `-y, --yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt.

## `piquelctl app secret access`

Change which environments, and whether previews, may mount a stored secret.

Options you omit keep the current access. Deployments that mount a secret they may no longer use fail with `secret_access_denied`; running ones keep their value. Needs `secrets:write`.

```text
piquelctl app secret <APPLICATION> access [OPTIONS] <NAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME>`: Secret name.

Options:

- `--environments <ENVIRONMENTS>`: Let only these environments mount the secret: comma-separated names or IDs, or `''` for none.
- `--all-environments`: Let every environment mount the secret, including ones created later.

  It never includes previews.
- `--previews`: Let previews mount the secret.
- `--no-previews`: Stop previews from mounting the secret.

## `piquelctl app secret delete`

Delete a stored secret and the Docker secrets made from it.

It fails while any environment's configuration or deployment still uses the secret. Needs `secrets:write`.

```text
piquelctl app secret <APPLICATION> delete [OPTIONS] <NAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME>`: Secret name.

Options:

- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Fail unless the secret is at this generation.

  Defaults to the generation it inspects.
- `-y, --yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt.

## `piquelctl app validate`

Check a TOML manifest locally, without contacting a daemon.

```text
piquelctl app validate [OPTIONS] --file <PATH>
```

Options:

- `--file <PATH>`: Manifest file: UTF-8 TOML of at most 2 MiB. Required.

## `piquelctl app plan`

Show what saving a TOML manifest would change, without saving it.

It exits with code 3 when the plan is blocked.

```text
piquelctl app plan [OPTIONS] --file <PATH>
```

Options:

- `--file <PATH>`: Manifest file: UTF-8 TOML of at most 2 MiB. Required.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Fail unless the application is at this generation; `0` requires that it doesn't exist.
- `--env <ENV>`: Render the manifest for this environment, and compare it with that environment's deployment.

  Defaults to the application's only environment. With several, the plan compares the manifest as written.

## `piquelctl app apply`

Save a TOML manifest, creating or replacing the application it names.

Without `--deploy`, it only saves the manifest. With it, it also deploys every environment that builds, and waits for each deployment.

```text
piquelctl app apply [OPTIONS] --file <PATH>
```

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--file <PATH>`: Manifest file: UTF-8 TOML of at most 2 MiB. Required.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Fail unless the application is at this generation; `0` requires that it doesn't exist.

  Defaults to the generation it inspects, or `0` when no application has the manifest's name.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt.
- `--force`: Replace whichever application has the manifest's name now, or create it.

  It skips the generation and identity checks, but still asks for confirmation.

## `piquelctl app delete`

Delete an application with all its environments and previews.

The environments' named volumes are kept; the previews' volumes are deleted. Needs `apps:delete`.

```text
piquelctl app delete [OPTIONS] <NAME_OR_ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME_OR_ID>`: Application name or stable ID.

Options:

- `--environments <NAMES>`: Names of all the application's environments, comma-separated.

  Required when it has several, to confirm that you delete them all.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Fail unless the application is at this generation.

  Defaults to the generation it inspects.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt.
- `--force`: Skip the generation check.

  It still asks for confirmation.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the daemon accepts the deletion, without waiting for it to end.

## `piquelctl app reconcile`

Retry the latest operation of the application's only environment.

It runs the operation again with its saved inputs, without fetching the manifest or resolving sources again. If the operation is still in progress, it waits for it instead. With several environments, use `env reconcile`. Needs `apps:deploy`.

```text
piquelctl app reconcile [OPTIONS] <NAME_OR_ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME_OR_ID>`: Application name or stable ID.

Options:

- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Fail unless the application is at this generation.

  Without it, a deployment uses the generation it inspects, and a retry checks none.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the daemon accepts the operation, without waiting for it to end.

## `piquelctl app deploy`

Deploy the application's only environment.

It fetches the manifest again, from the environment's branch for a repository-backed application, and resolves images and Git sources again. With several environments, use `env deploy`. Needs `apps:deploy`.

```text
piquelctl app deploy [OPTIONS] <NAME_OR_ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME_OR_ID>`: Application name or stable ID.

Options:

- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Fail unless the application is at this generation.

  Without it, a deployment uses the generation it inspects, and a retry checks none.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the daemon accepts the operation, without waiting for it to end.
- `--branch <BRANCH>`: Fetch the repository manifest from this branch, for this deployment only.

  The environment keeps following its own branch.
- `--commit <SHA>`: Fetch the repository manifest at this full commit hash, for this deployment only.

## `piquelctl app rename`

Rename an application.

It fails while an operation of the application is running, and for repository-backed applications, whose manifests set their name. Update `metadata.name` in your manifest files afterwards.

```text
piquelctl app rename [OPTIONS] <NAME_OR_ID> <NEW_NAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME_OR_ID>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<NEW_NAME>`: New name of the application, unused by any other.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.

## `piquelctl app manifest`

Print the saved manifest as TOML.

```text
piquelctl app manifest [OPTIONS] <NAME_OR_ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME_OR_ID>`: Application name or stable ID.

## `piquelctl app releases`

List the application's releases, newest first.

A release records what a deployment prepared: the manifest, and each service's image and where it came from.

```text
piquelctl app releases [OPTIONS] <NAME_OR_ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME_OR_ID>`: Application name or stable ID.

Options:

- `--cursor <CURSOR>`: Read the page after this cursor, which the previous page printed.

## `piquelctl env`

Create, inspect, deploy and delete an application's environments.

```text
piquelctl env [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Commands:

- [`piquelctl env list`](#piquelctl-env-list): List an application's environments and their status.
- [`piquelctl env create`](#piquelctl-env-create): Add an environment to an application.
- [`piquelctl env source`](#piquelctl-env-source): Make an environment receive releases promoted from another one, or build its own source again.
- [`piquelctl env promote`](#piquelctl-env-promote): Deploy a release into a promoted environment without building it.
- [`piquelctl env branch`](#piquelctl-env-branch): Point an environment at another branch of the manifest repository, or pin or unpin its commit.
- [`piquelctl env sync`](#piquelctl-env-sync): Choose whether pushes to an environment's branch deploy it.
- [`piquelctl env telemetry`](#piquelctl-env-telemetry): Grant an environment the daemon's telemetry, or revoke it.
- [`piquelctl env show`](#piquelctl-env-show): Show one environment, the manifest it deploys, and its status.
- [`piquelctl env visibility`](#piquelctl-env-visibility): Cap the visibility of an environment's routes in the saved manifest.
- [`piquelctl env rename`](#piquelctl-env-rename): Rename an environment without redeploying it.
- [`piquelctl env delete`](#piquelctl-env-delete): Delete an environment, keeping its named volumes.
- [`piquelctl env deploy`](#piquelctl-env-deploy): Deploy an environment from its source.
- [`piquelctl env reconcile`](#piquelctl-env-reconcile): Retry an environment's latest operation with the inputs it was given.
- [`piquelctl env secret`](#piquelctl-env-secret): List, regenerate, or delete an environment's generated secrets.
- [`piquelctl env logs`](#piquelctl-env-logs): Print the most recent lines of an environment's Docker logs.
- [`piquelctl env wait`](#piquelctl-env-wait): Wait until a deployment of an environment is ready.
- [`piquelctl env url`](#piquelctl-env-url): Print the URLs of an environment's routes, and whether each is ready.

## `piquelctl env list`

List an application's environments and their status.

Previews are not listed; use `preview list` for them.

```text
piquelctl env list [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION>
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.

## `piquelctl env create`

Add an environment to an application.

Nothing is deployed until you run `env deploy`, or `env promote` for a promoted environment. The environment deploys the application's saved manifest or, when the application is repository-backed, the manifest on its own branch.

You can't create an environment that the saved manifest has a `[spec.environments.<name>]` block for: saving the manifest creates it.

```text
piquelctl env create [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> <NAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<NAME>`: Name of the new environment, unique within the application: 1 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens, starting with a letter and ending with a letter or digit.

Options:

- `--branch <BRANCH>`: Branch of the manifest repository the environment follows. By default, the branch `spec.manifest` names. Only for repository-backed applications.
- `--commit <SHA>`: Deploy this commit of `--branch` instead of the branch's head: a full commit hash of 40 or 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
- `--promote-from <ENV>`: Make the environment promoted: it never builds, and only receives releases promoted from this environment of the application, given by name or stable ID, with `env promote`.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Change the environment only if the application's generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the command.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.
- `--force`: Change the environment even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.

## `piquelctl env source`

Make an environment receive releases promoted from another one, or build its own source again.

Nothing is deployed. A promoted environment never builds: it deploys what `env promote` sends it. When the saved manifest sets the environment's `promote_from`, `branch`, `commit` or `sync`, change it there instead.

```text
piquelctl env source [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> <ENVIRONMENT>
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<ENVIRONMENT>`: Environment name or stable ID.

Options:

- `--promote-from <ENV>`: Receive releases promoted from this environment of the application, given by name or stable ID.
- `--tracking`: Stop receiving promoted releases and build again: the saved manifest, or the branch `spec.manifest` names. Use `env branch` afterwards to follow another branch.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Change the environment only if the application's generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the command.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.
- `--force`: Change the environment even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.

## `piquelctl env promote`

Deploy a release into a promoted environment without building it.

By default, it deploys the release of the source environment's current deployment, which must have succeeded and be healthy now. The command asks for confirmation and waits for the deployment.

```text
piquelctl env promote [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> <ENVIRONMENT>
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<ENVIRONMENT>`: Name or stable ID of the promoted environment to deploy.

Options:

- `--deployment <ID>`: Promote the release of this deployment of the source environment. The command fails if it is no longer the source's current deployment.
- `--release <ID>`: Deploy this earlier release of the application instead, with the environment's current secrets.
- `--plan`: Show what would be deployed, and any secret it can't use, without deploying. The command exits with code 3 if the promotion would be refused. With `--release`, you can plan for any environment, promoted or not.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Fail unless the application is at this generation.

  Without it, a deployment uses the generation it inspects, and a retry checks none.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the daemon accepts the operation, without waiting for it to end.

## `piquelctl env branch`

Point an environment at another branch of the manifest repository, or pin or unpin its commit.

Only for repository-backed applications. Nothing is deployed: the environment's next deployment fetches the manifest from the new branch or commit. A promoted environment has no branch; use `env source --tracking` first. When the saved manifest sets the environment's `branch`, `commit`, `promote_from` or `sync`, change it there instead.

```text
piquelctl env branch [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> <ENVIRONMENT> <BRANCH>
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<ENVIRONMENT>`: Environment name or stable ID.
- `<BRANCH>`: Branch of the manifest repository the environment follows.

Options:

- `--commit <SHA>`: Deploy this commit of the branch instead of the branch's head: a full commit hash of 40 or 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Without it, the environment follows the branch's head, unpinning any commit.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Change the environment only if the application's generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the command.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.
- `--force`: Change the environment even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.

## `piquelctl env sync`

Choose whether pushes to an environment's branch deploy it.

This applies while the application's repository syncs (`app repository sync`). An environment that opts in deploys again whenever its branch moves past the head of its last deployment; one never deployed starts following from its first deployment. A pinned commit never follows pushes. When the saved manifest sets the environment's `sync`, `branch`, `commit` or `promote_from`, change it there instead. Opting in while the repository syncs needs the `apps:deploy` permission too.

```text
piquelctl env sync [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> <ENVIRONMENT> <on|off>
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<ENVIRONMENT>`: Environment name or stable ID.
- `<on|off>`: `on` deploys the environment when its branch moves; `off` deploys it only when you ask. Values: `on`, `off`.

## `piquelctl env telemetry`

Grant an environment the daemon's telemetry, or revoke it.

The receiving service of a granted environment, marked with `app service telemetry`, gets the traces, metrics and logs of every application. Revoking stops the export at once. Either way, the daemon mounts or unmounts the telemetry socket within seconds, which restarts the service; nothing is deployed. Both need the `telemetry:grant` permission. Previews are never granted.

```text
piquelctl env telemetry [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> <ENVIRONMENT> <on|off>
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<ENVIRONMENT>`: Environment name or stable ID.
- `<on|off>`: `on` grants the environment every application's telemetry; `off` revokes it. Values: `on`, `off`.

## `piquelctl env show`

Show one environment, the manifest it deploys, and its status.

```text
piquelctl env show [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> [ENVIRONMENT]
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `[ENVIRONMENT]`: Environment name or stable ID. You can omit it when the application has exactly one environment.

## `piquelctl env visibility`

Cap the visibility of an environment's routes in the saved manifest.

Each route gets the stricter of its own visibility and this cap. The cap is saved in the environment's `[spec.environments.<name>]` block. `private` adds the block when the manifest has none for the environment; `public`, which is no cap, only changes an existing one.

```text
piquelctl env visibility [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> <ENVIRONMENT> <VISIBILITY>
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<ENVIRONMENT>`: Environment name or stable ID.
- `<VISIBILITY>`: The strictest visibility the environment's routes get. `private` keeps every route on the tailnet; `public`, the default, restricts nothing. Values: `public`, `private`.

Options:

- `--deploy`: Also deploy the saved configuration.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the change is saved, or its deployment accepted, without waiting for the deployment to end.
- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Save only if the application's saved generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the save instead of being overwritten.
- `--force`: Save even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.

## `piquelctl env rename`

Rename an environment without redeploying it.

The command fails while the manifest the environment deploys, or the application's saved manifest, has a `[spec.environments.<name>]` block for the old or the new name.

```text
piquelctl env rename [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> <ENVIRONMENT> <NEW_NAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<ENVIRONMENT>`: Environment name or stable ID.
- `<NEW_NAME>`: New environment name, unique within the application: 1 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens, starting with a letter and ending with a letter or digit.

Options:

- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Change the environment only if the application's generation is still `GENERATION`. By default, it must still be the generation the command read, so a concurrent change fails the command.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.
- `--force`: Change the environment even if the application changed since the command read it. It still asks for confirmation.

## `piquelctl env delete`

Delete an environment, keeping its named volumes.

The command removes the environment's services and network, after confirmation, and waits until it is gone. To delete an environment that the saved manifest declares, remove its `[spec.environments.<name>]` block first.

```text
piquelctl env delete [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> <ENVIRONMENT>
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<ENVIRONMENT>`: Environment name or stable ID.

Options:

- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Fail unless the application is at this generation.

  Defaults to the generation it inspects.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt.
- `--force`: Skip the generation check.

  It still asks for confirmation.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the daemon accepts the deletion, without waiting for it to end.

## `piquelctl env deploy`

Deploy an environment from its source.

For a repository-backed application, it fetches the manifest from the environment's branch, or from `--branch` or `--commit` for this deployment only. Otherwise, it deploys the saved manifest. The command asks for confirmation and waits for the deployment. Promoted environments deploy with `env promote` instead.

```text
piquelctl env deploy [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> [ENVIRONMENT]
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `[ENVIRONMENT]`: Environment name or stable ID. You can omit it when the application has exactly one environment.

Options:

- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Fail unless the application is at this generation.

  Without it, a deployment uses the generation it inspects, and a retry checks none.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the daemon accepts the operation, without waiting for it to end.
- `--branch <BRANCH>`: Fetch the repository manifest from this branch, for this deployment only.

  The environment keeps following its own branch.
- `--commit <SHA>`: Fetch the repository manifest at this full commit hash, for this deployment only.

## `piquelctl env reconcile`

Retry an environment's latest operation with the inputs it was given.

If the operation is still in progress, the command waits for it instead of starting it again.

```text
piquelctl env reconcile [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> [ENVIRONMENT]
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `[ENVIRONMENT]`: Environment name or stable ID. You can omit it when the application has exactly one environment.

Options:

- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Fail unless the application is at this generation.

  Without it, a deployment uses the generation it inspects, and a retry checks none.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the daemon accepts the operation, without waiting for it to end.

## `piquelctl env secret`

List, regenerate, or delete an environment's generated secrets.

```text
piquelctl env secret [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> <COMMAND>
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.

Options:

- `--env <ENV>`: Environment name or stable ID. You can omit it when the application has exactly one environment.

Commands:

- [`piquelctl env secret list`](#piquelctl-env-secret-list): List the environment's generated secrets.
- [`piquelctl env secret regenerate`](#piquelctl-env-secret-regenerate): Generate a new value for a generated secret.
- [`piquelctl env secret delete`](#piquelctl-env-secret-delete): Delete a generated secret that nothing uses.

## `piquelctl env secret list`

List the environment's generated secrets.

It shows each secret's version, never its value.

```text
piquelctl env secret <APPLICATION> list [OPTIONS]
```

## `piquelctl env secret regenerate`

Generate a new value for a generated secret.

Use it to rotate a value, or to replace one that `secrets recover-key` discarded. The next deployment uses it; running services keep theirs until then. Needs `secrets:write`.

```text
piquelctl env secret <APPLICATION> regenerate [OPTIONS] <NAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME>`: Secret name.

Options:

- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Fail unless the secret is at this generation.

  Defaults to the generation it inspects.
- `-y, --yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt.

## `piquelctl env secret delete`

Delete a generated secret that nothing uses.

It fails while the configuration or a deployment still uses the secret. A later deployment that mounts it generates a new value. Needs `secrets:write`.

```text
piquelctl env secret <APPLICATION> delete [OPTIONS] <NAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME>`: Secret name.

Options:

- `--expected-generation <GENERATION>`: Fail unless the secret is at this generation.

  Defaults to the generation it inspects.
- `-y, --yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt.

## `piquelctl env logs`

Print the most recent lines of an environment's Docker logs.

```text
piquelctl env logs [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> [ENVIRONMENT]
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `[ENVIRONMENT]`: Environment name or stable ID. You can omit it when the application has exactly one environment.

Options:

- `--service <SERVICE>`: Only show this service's output.

  Defaults to every service.
- `--tail <TAIL>`: Show at most this many of the most recent lines, from 1 to 1000, merged across services. Default: `200`.
- `--since-seconds <SECONDS>`: Only show output written within this many seconds, from 1 to 86400 (a day). Default: `3600`.

## `piquelctl env wait`

Wait until a deployment of an environment is ready.

The command never follows a newer deployment. It exits with code 3 if a newer deployment or the environment's deletion supersedes it, 5 if it fails, and 4 when `--timeout` runs out. Builds usually take longer than the default `--timeout`.

```text
piquelctl env wait [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> [ENVIRONMENT]
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `[ENVIRONMENT]`: Environment name or stable ID. You can omit it when the application has exactly one environment.

Options:

- `--deployment <ID>`: ID of the deployment to wait for. By default, the latest deployment when the command starts.
- `--ready <READY>`: How ready the deployment must be before the command returns. Default: `runtime`.
  - `runtime`: The deployment succeeded, and the daemon observes every service healthy.
  - `routes`: As `runtime`, and every URL of its routes is ready.

## `piquelctl env url`

Print the URLs of an environment's routes, and whether each is ready.

```text
piquelctl env url [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> [ENVIRONMENT]
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `[ENVIRONMENT]`: Environment name or stable ID. You can omit it when the application has exactly one environment.

Options:

- `--route <NAME>`: Print only the URL of the route with this name, with a warning while it is pending.

## `piquelctl preview`

Create, inspect, deploy and delete previews: disposable deployments of a branch.

```text
piquelctl preview [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Commands:

- [`piquelctl preview create`](#piquelctl-preview-create): Create a preview of a branch and deploy it.
- [`piquelctl preview deploy`](#piquelctl-preview-deploy): Deploy the head of a preview's branch again, or a snapshot of your Git worktree with `--local`.
- [`piquelctl preview list`](#piquelctl-preview-list): List an application's previews with their status and branch state.
- [`piquelctl preview show`](#piquelctl-preview-show): Show one preview, its URLs, and the state of its branch.
- [`piquelctl preview logs`](#piquelctl-preview-logs): Print the most recent lines of a preview's Docker logs.
- [`piquelctl preview wait`](#piquelctl-preview-wait): Wait until a deployment of a preview is ready.
- [`piquelctl preview url`](#piquelctl-preview-url): Print the URLs of a preview's routes, and whether each is ready.
- [`piquelctl preview exec`](#piquelctl-preview-exec): Run a one-off command in a running task of a preview's service, streaming its output.
- [`piquelctl preview delete`](#piquelctl-preview-delete): Delete a preview and every volume it created.
- [`piquelctl preview prune`](#piquelctl-preview-prune): Delete the previews whose branch is gone from the repository.

## `piquelctl preview create`

Create a preview of a branch and deploy it.

Only for repository-backed applications. If the preview of that branch and slot already exists, the command shows it and its latest deployment without deploying it again. It fails when a new preview would exceed the daemon's preview limits.

```text
piquelctl preview create [OPTIONS] --branch <BRANCH> <APPLICATION>
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.

Options:

- `--branch <BRANCH>`: Branch of the manifest repository to deploy. Required.
- `--slot <SLOT>`: Distinguishes several previews of one branch, such as one per agent: 1 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens, starting with a letter and ending with a letter or digit.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the daemon accepts the deployment, without waiting for it to finish.

## `piquelctl preview deploy`

Deploy the head of a preview's branch again, or a snapshot of your Git worktree with `--local`.

Deploying the branch's head replaces a local snapshot the preview runs.

```text
piquelctl preview deploy [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> [PREVIEW]
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `[PREVIEW]`: Preview ID, slug, or branch. Omit it with `--local`.

Options:

- `--slot <SLOT>`: The preview's slot. Give it to address a preview with a slot by its branch, or to choose the preview `--local` deploys to.
- `--local`: Deploy a snapshot of the Git worktree of the current directory, without pushing it.

  The snapshot has the worktree's committed, uncommitted, and untracked files. Ignored files are left out, or sent as committed when they are tracked. The command lists the uncommitted files it sends, and deploys to the preview of the current branch and `--slot`, creating it if needed. Your repository is never changed. A large first upload may need a longer `--timeout`.
- `--full-history`: Upload every commit of `HEAD` with the snapshot.

  By default, the command sends only the commits since the nearest ancestor of `HEAD` that a remote-tracking branch has, and the daemon fetches that ancestor from the application's repository. Use this when there is no such ancestor, or the daemon can't fetch it.
- `--branch <BRANCH>`: Deploy the snapshot as the preview of this branch instead of the current one. Required when `HEAD` is detached.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the daemon accepts the deployment, without waiting for it to finish.

## `piquelctl preview list`

List an application's previews with their status and branch state.

```text
piquelctl preview list [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION>
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.

## `piquelctl preview show`

Show one preview, its URLs, and the state of its branch.

The branch is `exists`, `moved` (past the deployed commit), `gone`, `local` (the preview runs or is deploying a local snapshot), or `unknown` (the repository can't be read).

```text
piquelctl preview show [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> <PREVIEW>
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<PREVIEW>`: Preview ID, slug, or branch, matched in that order.

Options:

- `--slot <SLOT>`: The preview's slot. Needed to address a preview with a slot by its branch.

## `piquelctl preview logs`

Print the most recent lines of a preview's Docker logs.

```text
piquelctl preview logs [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> <PREVIEW>
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<PREVIEW>`: Preview ID, slug, or branch, matched in that order.

Options:

- `--slot <SLOT>`: The preview's slot. Needed to address a preview with a slot by its branch.
- `--service <SERVICE>`: Only show this service's output.

  Defaults to every service.
- `--tail <TAIL>`: Show at most this many of the most recent lines, from 1 to 1000, merged across services. Default: `200`.
- `--since-seconds <SECONDS>`: Only show output written within this many seconds, from 1 to 86400 (a day). Default: `3600`.

## `piquelctl preview wait`

Wait until a deployment of a preview is ready.

The command never follows a newer deployment. It exits with code 3 if a newer deployment or the preview's deletion supersedes it, 5 if it fails, and 4 when `--timeout` runs out. Builds usually take longer than the default `--timeout`.

```text
piquelctl preview wait [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> <PREVIEW>
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<PREVIEW>`: Preview ID, slug, or branch, matched in that order.

Options:

- `--slot <SLOT>`: The preview's slot. Needed to address a preview with a slot by its branch.
- `--deployment <ID>`: ID of the deployment to wait for. By default, the latest deployment when the command starts.
- `--ready <READY>`: How ready the deployment must be before the command returns. Default: `runtime`.
  - `runtime`: The deployment succeeded, and the daemon observes every service healthy.
  - `routes`: As `runtime`, and every URL of its routes is ready.

## `piquelctl preview url`

Print the URLs of a preview's routes, and whether each is ready.

```text
piquelctl preview url [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> <PREVIEW>
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<PREVIEW>`: Preview ID, slug, or branch, matched in that order.

Options:

- `--slot <SLOT>`: The preview's slot. Needed to address a preview with a slot by its branch.
- `--route <NAME>`: Print only the URL of the route with this name, with a warning while it is pending.

## `piquelctl preview exec`

Run a one-off command in a running task of a preview's service, streaming its output.

`piquelctl` exits with the command's exit code. `--timeout` limits each request, not the session.

```text
piquelctl preview exec [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> <PREVIEW> <SERVICE> -- <COMMAND>...
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<PREVIEW>`: Preview ID, slug, or branch, matched in that order.
- `<SERVICE>`: Service that runs the command, in one of its running tasks.
- `<COMMAND>...`: Program to run and its arguments, after `--`.

Options:

- `--slot <SLOT>`: The preview's slot. Needed to address a preview with a slot by its branch.
- `-i, --interactive`: Forward standard input to the command.
- `-t, --tty`: Allocate a terminal, for interactive programs such as a shell.

  It implies `--interactive`, and needs a terminal on standard input, which it switches to raw mode so that keys such as Ctrl-C reach the command.

## `piquelctl preview delete`

Delete a preview and every volume it created.

The volumes' data is lost. The command asks for confirmation and waits until the preview is gone.

```text
piquelctl preview delete [OPTIONS] <APPLICATION> <PREVIEW>
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.
- `<PREVIEW>`: Preview ID, slug, or branch, matched in that order.

Options:

- `--slot <SLOT>`: The preview's slot. Needed to address a preview with a slot by its branch.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the daemon accepts the deletion, without waiting for it to finish.

## `piquelctl preview prune`

Delete the previews whose branch is gone from the repository.

The command lists them and asks for confirmation. The daemon checks each branch again and keeps any preview it can no longer confirm is gone. Previews whose branch state is `unknown` or `local` are kept. Their volumes are deleted with them.

```text
piquelctl preview prune [OPTIONS] --branch-gone <APPLICATION>
```

Arguments:

- `<APPLICATION>`: Application name or stable ID.

Options:

- `--branch-gone`: Select the previews whose branch no longer exists. Required. Required.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt. You need it when not on a terminal.
- `--no-wait`: Return once the daemon accepts the deletion, without waiting for it to finish.

## `piquelctl builds`

Inspect Git source builds and job runs, and read their output.

```text
piquelctl builds [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Commands:

- [`piquelctl builds list`](#piquelctl-builds-list): List Git source builds and job runs, newest first.
- [`piquelctl builds logs`](#piquelctl-builds-logs): Read the newest page of a build's output.

## `piquelctl builds list`

List Git source builds and job runs, newest first.

```text
piquelctl builds list [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--application <APPLICATION_ID>`: Only show the builds of the environments of the application with this ID.
- `--environment <ENVIRONMENT_ID>`: Only show the builds of the environment with this ID.
- `--cursor <CURSOR>`: Read the page after this cursor, which the previous page printed.

## `piquelctl builds logs`

Read the newest page of a build's output.

To read older output, pass the `--before` offset it prints. Needs `logs:read`.

```text
piquelctl builds logs [OPTIONS] <ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<ID>`: Build ID, from `builds list`.

Options:

- `--before <OFFSET>`: Read the output before this byte offset, which the previous page printed.

## `piquelctl operation`

Show an operation, waiting until it ends.

Deployments, deletions and other long tasks run as operations, whose IDs commands print. Unless you pass `--no-wait`, it exits with code 5 if the operation failed.

```text
piquelctl operation [OPTIONS] <OPERATION_ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<OPERATION_ID>`: Operation ID.

Options:

- `--no-wait`: Show the operation's current state instead of waiting for it to end.

## `piquelctl events`

Read one page of the event history, oldest first.

Events record what happened to applications, environments and the daemon, such as edits, deployments and failures.

```text
piquelctl events [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--application <APPLICATION_ID>`: Only show events of the application with this ID, and of all its environments, including deleted ones.
- `--environment <ENVIRONMENT_ID>`: Only show events of the environment with this ID, even a deleted one.
- `--cursor <CURSOR>`: Read the page after this cursor, which the previous page printed.
- `--limit <LIMIT>`: Show at most this many events, from 1 to 100. Default: `50`.
